summary: The sole occurrence fits inherited II.1 beschmieren and matches the inherited Preterit quotation. Its longer lead-in adds narrative setting but no independent stem, box or sense; no example is added.
The Preterit has -le with l-marked lu taʕlo as agent; affected foṯe du dewo w qarʕe is unmarked, and b- introduces the applied substance ṭino. lu taʕlo must not be treated as a recipient.
The input reference PrS 74/63 and inherited prs 215/23 identify matching wording under different reference systems. The supplied evidence cannot determine the mapping; no fix-citation is proposed.
The edition uses Kot; the reader’s English mud is an analytical paraphrase and does not replace the inherited German quotation.
Round 2 is based on the supplied Jan Turoyo; accompanying English is project machine translation [MT]. Round 1 was read first and its proposals are not duplicated.

Jan 2.5/1583 places ləbxiwo ʕayne dan naʕime between kohl application and mlaṭšiwonne. The semantic alternatives are holding eyes for application, rubbing, or smearing; the Turoyo sequence does not identify which operation the bare form itself names.
The inherited glossary and round 1 have only II mlabaxle/mlabəx beschmieren. The Jan form lacks m-, so it does not securely establish a new I or a reduced II paradigm on one ambiguous passage.

Form lookup retrieves lbx as a candidate. The separate lbk entry has occupation/busying senses, not a direct evidence-backed solution for this x-final form. No reassignment to lbk or source emendation is proposed.

The -iwo ending is consistent with plural Infectum-wa; that morphological observation alone cannot settle the lexical root/stem analysis. No new box, numbered sense, idiom or duplicate old correction is added.
Reconcile PrS 74/63 with inherited prs 215/23 and confirm the relevant edition/page-versus-text numbering before changing the citation.
Further attestations could establish whether the affected surface is consistently unmarked and the applied substance consistently introduced by b-.
At Jan 2.5/1583, what precisely does ləbxiwo do to the children’s eyes: hold them, rub them, or smear kohl?
Is ləbxiwo an independent I formation, reduced II, or another lexeme? Obtain base forms and speaker confirmation before adding a new stem.
